A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Flexora and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Content can be reliably matched despite pagination and display-placement changes.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark evaluations and ablations in Section 5, additional experiments in Appendix C, numerical smoothness results in Appendix E, and model-output cases in Appendix G.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, numerical experiments, and model-output cases in Section 5 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The three-stage method, continuous relaxation, alternating optimization, positive-alpha layer selection, and retraining of selected adapters remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is relocated without changing its steps.

E1.justification: Both versions retain HellaSwag, PIQA, Winogrande, and RACE evaluations, plus the BoolQ, ARC-e, ARC-c, and OBQA comparisons in Appendix C.4. No dataset or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 1 and the appendix comparisons, including full fine-tuning, LoRA variants, random layer selection, and LoRAShear. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The splits, prompt processing, accuracy metric, model configurations, and training settings in Section 5.1 and Appendix B are retained. Table 5 already contains both LoRA epoch controls and Flexora's 1+3-epoch schedule in v4.

E4.justification: Both retain the layer-selection, fine-tuning-stage, and training-duration ablations; rank, search-sample, and K/T analyses; loss and smoothness analyses; and Appendix G case studies. Relocated displays do not introduce new analyses.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains three random layer selections and their average, while Appendix E.2 retains averaging over ten sampled inputs. Run/seed disclosures and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged; neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results, plotted findings, and Appendix G outputs are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same average accuracies of 86.46% for Flexora at rank 8 and 83.04% for LoRA at rank 8 in both versions.

T1.justification: The HPO formulation, Propositions 1–2, cited Theorem 1, smoothness definition, and proofs and derivations in Appendices A and E are unchanged. Mathematical spacing differences do not alter their content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about automatic layer selection through HPO and unrolled differentiation, reduced parameters and overfitting, scalability, and improved performance.

C2.justification: The overfitting, critical-layer, and smoothness interpretations remain unchanged, as do limitations concerning insufficient validation samples and incompatibility with some LoRA variants. Added citations do not revise these explanations or qualifications.

D1.justification: Both retain the same prompt templates, hyperparameters, selected-layer lists, training/search timings, Llama-factory and OpenCompass disclosures, and NVIDIA A100 hardware information. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: v5 adds references to PAFT (Wei et al., 2025a) in Section 1, ReDiT (2025c) in Section 3.1, and TMPO (2025b) in Appendix F. These are limited citation additions; the related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are limited to the updated arXiv version/date header and minor spacing adjustments. The prose, terminology, section sequence, and appendix organization are otherwise retained, apart from the citation insertions.

P2.justification: Display placement and spacing change: Algorithm 1 moves from PDF page 4 to page 5, and Tables 4–5 move from page 8 to page 9. The same 22 tables and 15 figures remain, with unchanged captions and graphical content.

improvement.justification: v5 adds three citations and reflows existing material, while retaining the same method, experimental evidence, mathematical arguments, explanations, and reproducibility information. These limited bibliographic and presentation changes do not produce a meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
